title: Jones Beach

description.main: Joseph Szabo's photographs of the crowds at Jones Beach on Long Island, made from the early 1970s, with an introduction by Vince Aletti.
description.extended:
A survey of Jones Beach, the Long Island public beach, as seen by Joseph Szabo over some thirty-five years of photographing its crowds.

Szabo began the project in the early 1970s, at a beach the publisher says draws more than six million visitors a year. The pictures show muscle men, displays of beachwear, oiled skin, sprayed hair and shy adolescents, with moments of quiet and of exuberance. Vince Aletti contributes an introduction. The book runs to 112 pages in a square format.

Szabo (b. 1944) studied at Pratt Institute (MFA, 1968) and taught photography at Malverne High School on Long Island from 1972 to 1999, and at the International Center of Photography in New York. His earlier books are Almost Grown (Harmony Books, 1978) and Teenage (Greybull Press, 2003), both about adolescence.
